name: Serin Ngai
tagline: Top rated Family Law attorney in Seattle, Washington
about: Serin Ngai is a family law attorney in Seattle, Washington with over 19 years of experience. The founder of her own firm, Sound Family Solutions PLLC, Ms. Ngai represents clients in Greater Seattle and throughout King County. She handles a wide variety of family law cases including divorce, parenting plans (child custody), child support, spousal maintenance, post-divorce matters, prenuptial/postnuptial agreements, and same-sex family law matters, to name a few.

Ms. Ngai focuses her practice on cooperative and collaborative methods to obtain out of court settlement agreements to enable her clients to resolve their family disputes in a non-adversarial setting, and where they have the most control over the outcomes. She concentrates on finding efficient solutions that are in the best interest of her clients while continuing to strongly advocate on their behalf. She is also certified in Collaborative Law and resolves cases using this statutory out-of-court process. Past clients have praised her for her prompt communication, advocacy, writing, and finding creative solutions to resolve their family disputes.

In addition to representing private clients, Ms. Ngai is a certified Guardian ad Litem on the King County Title 26 Guardian Ad Litem Registry. In this role, she is appointed by the court to investigate, analyze, and recommend what is in the best interests of the children in family law disputes. This experience provides her with a distinct advantage in her own parenting cases.

Active in the Asian Bar Association of Washington for over 15 consecutive years, Ms. Ngai served as President of the Association in 2020. In 2017, she received the Association’s Pro Bono Award for her volunteer work with the organization’s legal clinic and long-term service to the Association. In 2025, Ms. Ngai served as President of the Asian Bar Association of Washington Student Scholarship Foundation. She also volunteers at legal clinics for the past 18 years.

After earning a bachelor's degree from the University of Washington, Ms. Ngai graduated from Seattle University School of Law. While in law school, she was Managing Editor of the Seattle Journal for Social Justice where her article on an arts education was published. She was also honored with several academic awards.
